extracted.intended_audience: news publishers, news consumers, and NewsGuard users (analysts/readers seeking to understand website ratings)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for assessing the credibility and transparency of news and information websites using NewsGuard’s nine apolitical journalistic criteria to produce a 0–100 score and a Nutrition Label explaining the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does not publish false or egregiously misleading content at a significant level
rubrics_metrics.description: The site does not produce false or egregiously misleading content at a level that, in NewsGuard’s judgment, signifies a clear disregard for factual accuracy—i.e., a visitor to the site risks being significantly misled on important topics. (22 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Details: reasons to pass include no evidence of publishing false or egregiously misleading content, only minor factual errors, quick/transparent corrections of major mistakes, and lack of recent significant false content. Reasons to fail include publishing false or egregiously misleading content at a level likely to mislead visitors, featuring past significant false content in prominent places, asserting claims contradicted by abundant scientific evidence, promoting baseless conspiracy theories, and presenting others' false claims as fact without context. Note: NewsGuard reviews factual statements in news and opinion pieces for this criterion (opinions not rated on opinion content alone).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathers and presents information responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Content providers are generally fair and accurate in reporting and presenting information: they reference multiple sources (preferably direct/firsthand), avoid egregious distortion, and do not misrepresent information to make an argument. (18 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Details: pass indicators include factual reporting in context, clear attribution to credible sources, verifiable claims, noting when quoted sources are false or unsubstantiated, lack of repeated false/unsubstantiated claims, and adequate oversight of AI-generated content. Fail indicators include egregious distortion (e.g., quotes out of context), repeated false content, routinely quoting false/unsubstantiated sources without noting issues, leaving older clearly false claims online uncorrected, one-sided coverage without disclosure of ownership/finance-driven perspective, poor sourcing or omission of context (times/places/names), routine republication without attribution, reliance on anonymous sources without context, and undisclosed/unsupervised AI-generated content that produces egregious errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has effective practices for correcting errors
rubrics_metrics.description: The site regularly identifies errors and publishes clarifications and corrections, transparently acknowledges errors, and does not regularly leave significant false content uncorrected. (12.5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Details: pass indicators include a regular practice of corrections (at least one correction per year), visible and clearly described corrections, and acceptable absence of corrections for very new sites with no found false claims. The existence of a corrections policy is not required to pass. Fail indicators include not regularly issuing corrections, deleting or silently editing inaccurate content instead of issuing transparent corrections, lack of corrections in the last 12 months despite prior corrections, only correcting as a result of NewsGuard’s review, or repeatedly leaving significant false claims uncorrected even if minor errors are corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handles the difference between news and opinion responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Content providers who convey news or a mix of news and opinion clearly distinguish opinion from news reporting; when reporting news they do not egregiously cherry-pick facts to advance opinions; outlets that advance a particular viewpoint disclose that point of view. (12.5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Details: pass indicators include clearly labeled opinion sections (e.g., “opinion,” “editorial”), signaling opinion by author name formatting, prominent disclosure of a site’s perspective if it advances an overall agenda, news content free of opinionated language, or a site that clearly and consistently identifies itself as opinion-only. Fail indicators include news content with frequent opinionated language, advancing a viewpoint through one-sided story selection without disclosure, mixing news and opinion without clear distinction, and inaccurate labeling of news/opinion. Sites that are clearly the website of an advocacy organization and are transparent about their mission may receive N/A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids deceptive headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The site generally does not publish headlines that include false information, significantly sensationalize, or otherwise misrepresent the content under the headline. (10 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Details: pass indicators include accurate factual headlines that properly communicate article content and occasional buzzy headlines that do not misrepresent facts. A site with some deceptive headlines may still pass if such headlines are infrequent. Fail indicators include frequent headlines that do not reflect the content or that contain significant falsehoods. Sites that do not publish headlines may receive N/A for this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website discloses ownership and financing
rubrics_metrics.description: The site discloses in a user-friendly manner its ownership and/or financing and any notable political affiliations or financial interests relevant to the site’s coverage, so readers know who is funding the content and potential interests of owners/funders. (7.5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Details: pass indicators include clear identification of owners in a prominent, accessible section; disclosure of owners’ or funders’ notable political/financial affiliations that may present conflicts; disclosure in specific stories when relevant; and identification of major donors for nonprofit-owned sites. Fail indicators include not clearly identifying owner/parent company, only listing owner info where an average user would not look (e.g., copyright/terms page), failing to identify major donors for nonprofits, and failing to disclose potential conflicts of interest involving owners/funders in related stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly labels advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: The site makes clear which content is paid for and which is not, distinguishing advertising from editorial content with clear visual cues or explicit labels that the average reader would understand. (7.5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Details: pass indicators include explicit labels such as “advertisement,” “paid content,” “sponsored,” prominent disclosure at the start or headline of sponsored articles, disclosure of commercial content-sharing arrangements, and clear affiliate-link disclosures accessible to average readers. Fail indicators include presenting sponsored/promotional articles alongside editorial content without clear distinction, embedding affiliate links without clear disclosure, labeling commercial content with confusing terms (e.g., “From Our Partners”) that an average reader would not understand as paid, or running promotional articles without disclosing the commercial relationship. Sites that do not publish advertisements or sponsored content may receive N/A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveals who’s in charge, including possible conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Those in charge of the content are identified on the site and there is a way for readers to contact the site about editorial issues—i.e., the reader is told who decides what content is published. (5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Details: pass indicators include clear identification of an editorial lead in an easily accessible section and contact methods for editorial issues, and disclosure of significant potential conflicts of interest of editorial leaders. Fail indicators include not identifying someone who oversees editorial content or only doing so in an inaccessible place, listing an editorial lead without any contact method, or failing to disclose significant conflicts of interest of editorial leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: The site provides the names of content creators, along with either contact or biographical information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about those producing the content is accessible; it is generally clear who produces which content and authors have full names plus either contact information or relevant biographical details. (5 Points)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Details: pass indicators include bylines with full names and contact/biographical information for most content creators, or a staff directory listing names, bios, contact info, and coverage areas; disclosure if content is regularly AI-produced. Fail indicators include rare or no bylines, bylines with only first names/initials/pseudonyms, attribution without contact/biographical info, or undisclosed AI-generated content attributed to human writers. Note: NewsGuard recognizes safety/privacy concerns for journalists in dangerous contexts, and that can affect scoring (e.g., 95 vs. 100 Green score).

rubrics_metrics.name: Score and Rating Levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites receive a 0–100 score (expressed as 0%–100%) based on the weighted sum of the nine criteria; scores map to rating-level language that explains the degree of adherence to standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score-to-label mapping: 100 — 'High Credibility' (adheres to all nine standards); 75–99 — 'Generally Credible' (mostly adheres); 60–74 — 'Credible with Exceptions' (generally maintains standards with significant exceptions); 40–59 — 'Proceed with Caution' (unreliable because it fails several standards); 0–39 — 'Proceed with Maximum Caution' (unreliable because it severely violates standards). Nutrition Labels explain how the score was arrived at and provide evidence/examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special categories: Satire and Platform (not scored using nine criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some websites are not scored with the nine criteria because the criteria are not directly relevant; these sites receive a Nutrition Label describing the site generally rather than a numeric score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire: humor or satire sites that are not traditional news outlets receive a 'satire' rating and are described (including who is behind it when possible) rather than scored. Platform: sites that primarily host user-published content with limited vetting, are presented so typical readers recognize content is not vetted, and do not publish significant original content receive a 'platform' rating and a description rather than a numeric score. Such sites may still be described in Nutrition Labels regarding practices and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring rules: pass-fail, weighted points, and N/A allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the nine criteria is applied on a pass-fail basis: a site either receives all the points for a criterion or none; criteria are weighted (points add to 100); in some specific cases a criterion may be marked N/A and the publisher receives the points associated with that criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NewsGuard uses pass-fail to enable scalable human ratings across thousands of sites; this can reduce precision but partial-credit alternatives are not feasible. When a criterion does not apply, NewsGuard may mark it N/A and award the points. Satire/platform categories are excluded from scoring. All scoring decisions and point allocations are documented in a site's Nutrition Label with evidence and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring process and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The process by which ratings are produced: trained NewsGuard analysts research and assess sites against the nine criteria, draft a Nutrition Label, seek comment from the publisher, and have the score reviewed and fact-checked by senior editors and co-CEOs before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process details: analysts are trained journalists who report to determine ownership, financing, credibility, and transparency; Nutrition Labels include a grid of judgments and written explanation with evidence; NewsGuard calls websites for comment when a site may fail criteria and includes publisher comments in the assessment; at least one senior editor and NewsGuard’s co-CEOs review every Nutrition Label; scores are apolitical and based solely on the nine criteria; NewsGuard periodically updates scores and documents changes in editor’s notes; Nutrition Labels list the writer and editors for accountability; publishers can submit complaints and responses which NewsGuard will publish and link from the Nutrition Label.
